name: Rhombus
description: A star 50 parsecs away, 13 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 19780: radius 12.812 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 103.911 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.049) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 19780: effective temperature 5152 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.04)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 19780: distance 49.554 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.005), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 50 parsecs away, 13 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 104 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,152 K, so 12.812 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 19780: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Alpha Reticuli
quotes.card: Alpha Reticuli, Latinized from α Reticuli, also named Rhombus, is the brightest star in the southern circumpolar constellation of Reticulum, with an apparent visual magnitude of 3.3.
quotes.introduction: This appears to be a solitary star located at a distance of 160 light-years from Earth.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 4676528209144882304 (quality A), from 2015A&A...574A..50J; Gaia DR3 measures none
